detail.longDescription: I am currently working on an application where we get an email, and after identification, we process that email with AI, where a response is required in JSON format for the values. Initially, I used a strict JSON schema technique, but I faced challenges with timeouts and blank-line output from the OpenAI model gpt-4o-mini . I also found that over-contexting is causing problems in response generation. Sometimes it misses the row that I want to process, and sometimes it totally misses the present value. I cut the over-contexted prompt, reduced its size, and changed from Strict JSON schema to Sparse JSON schema so now it has improved the response as only the fact values are returned and the response improved, but it still misses the values. I am looking for a solution on how to restrict the response so that the AI misses fewer values, and the reason for using the model is that the only required work for the AI is to read the values and put them into the field where they belong. There will be no specific email pattern; we can get any email in any kind of format, and it can also be in a document and directly in the body. Model Settings: - Model: gpt-4o-mini - temperature: 0.1 - max_completion_tokens: 3000 - response_format: json_schema (strict: true) - stream: true - timeout: 240s The following is my example Prompt with a synthesized business use case in which I am facing the problem. Simplified example (my real prompt is ~27K characters; this is a reduced version with the same structure) Prompt (trimmed): You read one reply from a service provider to a price request and report what the provider wrote, exactly as written, as structured data. RULES 1. Use only what is written in the SOURCE. Never use outside knowledge. Never infer, assume or guess. 2. Return exactly one entry in "items" for every item in ITEMS ASKED, using its number as "item_no". 3. A null is a normal answer and far better than a guessed value. But when the provider DID write a value, report it, even if it came in an unusual form or sits inside a longer sentence. 4. Every field is an object {value, confidence, quote, location}. "quote" is the exact words copied from the SOURCE that show the value. If there is no quote, the value is null. 5. Do not calculate, convert or tidy anything beyond what a field description says. FIELDS (per item) - unit_price: the price for one unit as written, number only. - currency: ISO code of the price (USD, EUR, GBP...). - lead_time_days: notice or delivery time in days. "2 weeks" = 14. Null if not written. - valid_until: the date the offer is valid until, as written. Null if not written. - payment_terms: the payment terms the provider wrote for this item, for example "Net 30", "50% advance", "payment on delivery". They can be in the table row, a notes column or the footer. - conditions: any other condition written for this item (warranty, deposit, exclusions). Schema (trimmed, every field is an object): { "items": [{ "item_no": {"value": "integer", "confidence": "number|null", "quote": "string|null", "location": "string|null"}, "unit_price": {"value": "number|null", "confidence": "number|null", "quote": "string|null", "location": "string|null"}, "currency": {"value": "string|null", "confidence": "number|null", "quote": "string|null", "location": "string|null"}, "lead_time_days": {"value": "integer|null", "confidence": "number|null", "quote": "string|null", "location": "string|null"}, "valid_until": {"value": "string|null", "confidence": "number|null", "quote": "string|null", "location": "string|null"}, "payment_terms": {"value": "string|null", "confidence": "number|null", "quote": "string|null", "location": "string|null"}, "conditions": {"value": "string|null", "confidence": "number|null", "quote": "string|null", "location": "string|null"} }] } ITEMS ASKED (sent with the prompt): 1. Conference hall hire, 1 day, 200 guests 2. Catering, lunch buffet, 200 guests 3. Sound and projector package, 1 day Source (provider email; the provider answered inside a copy of our request table): Hi, thanks for the enquiry. Please find our rates below. Item | Price | Booking notice | Offer valid | Terms 1 | USD 2,400 | 3 weeks | 30 Nov 2026 | Net 30, 2-year cancellation policy 2 | USD 18 pp | 10 days | 30 Nov 2026 | 50% advance, rest on the event day 3 | USD 650 | 5 days | 15 Nov 2026 | Net 30, technician included Prices exclude VAT. Expected: item 1: 2400 USD, 21 days, valid 30 Nov 2026, payment_terms "Net 30" item 2: 18 USD, 10 days, valid 30 Nov 2026, payment_terms "50% advance, rest on the event day" item 3: 650 USD, 5 days, valid 15 Nov 2026, payment_terms "Net 30" Actual (gpt-4o-mini, temperature 0.1, strict json_schema): item 1: 2400 USD, 21 days, valid 30 Nov 2026, payment_terms item 2: , 10 days, valid 30 Nov 2026, payment_terms What I tried: Strict JSON schema: timeouts and blank-line output until max tokens Smaller prompt and a sparse schema (only fields found are returned): cleaner output, but values are still missed temperature 0.1, max_completion_tokens 3000, stream true I tried multiple approaches to resolve the query but it get fails multiple times, I am looking for a better approach where I can get the accurate response from AI most of the time so failure rates for the extraction could be dropped. A point to mention I am using human in the loop concept on the basis of AI confidence on the extraction field, incase of 90% or more I accept its response automatically or otherwise it goes into review.
